title: Hotfix: disable fused INT8 dequant+GEMM path on L40S (intermittent correctness)
author: Grace Kim
release_notes:
- Hotfix: disable fused INT8 dequant+GEMM kernel on NVIDIA L40S due to intermittent correctness failures; fallback to unfused path on affected GPUs.
- Added GPU-conditional guard + override flag for controlled re-enable in perf lab only.
body:
Context: After enabling the fused INT8 dequant+GEMM path (introduced in the recent INT8 optimization work), we observed intermittent correctness failures on NVIDIA L40S in both perf-lab soak runs and one customer report (SUP-6194). Failures present as rare but large token-level divergence vs FP16 baseline on otherwise stable prompts; not a consistent numerical drift issue.

Impact: This is a correctness risk on a production GPU SKU (L40S) and should not ship with the current release train.

Root cause (current hypothesis): The fused kernel variant used on SM89 (L40S) appears sensitive to specific M/N/K shapes + alignment constraints in the decode loop (likely vectorized load alignment / epilogue accumulator path). We have not isolated the minimal kernel bug yet; this PR is deliberately scoped as a safe hotfix.

Fix: GPU-conditional disable of the fused INT8 dequant+GEMM path on L40S (SM89). We keep the fused path enabled on H100/H200/A100 where we have not reproduced the issue. On L40S we fall back to the prior unfused implementation (dequant + GEMM). Added a runtime knob to override the guard for perf experiments in perf-lab only.

Behavioral changes: Only affects INT8 execution when the fused path would be selected; FP8/FP16 paths unchanged. Performance on L40S INT8 may regress relative to the fused path, but correctness is prioritized.

Testing:
- Added a targeted regression test that runs the affected shape set (captured from benchmark logs) and asserts max-abs / top-k token match thresholds vs FP16 baseline.
- Verified guard triggers on L40S and does not trigger on H100.
- Ran short soak (30 min) in perf-lab on L40S with the guard enabled; no divergences observed.

Rollout/ops:
- This is intended for release/2025.10 hotfix. Once merged, release eng can cherry-pick/squash into the release candidate if needed.
- Override flag should remain undocumented for customers; intended for internal A/B only.

Follow-ups (out of scope here):
- Isolate the fused kernel bug on SM89 via microbench + alignment assertions.
- Add a capability table entry so kernel auto-selection avoids the fused variant on SM89 until re-validated.
- Extend correctness soak coverage for L40S in perf-canary (ENG-24819).
commits: runtime/quant: add SM89 (L40S) guard to disable fused int8 dequant+gemm
tests/quant: add regression for l40s intermittent divergence shape set
docs/internal: note hotfix rationale in release checklist
conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we make the guard explicit to L40S rather than all SM89? Also want an override for perf-lab experiments, but it must default to safe.
Grace Kim (author): Updated to check device name contains "L40S" OR (SM89 && vendor=NVIDIA && sku_class=workstation) to avoid surprising behavior on other Ada SKUs; default remains disabled. Added internal override flag gated behind "--allow-unsafe-flags".

Arjun Desai (review): For the regression test, please ensure we compare against FP16 with deterministic decoding params (temperature=0, top_p=1). Also add a note that this is not an accuracy eval; it’s a divergence guard.
Grace Kim (author): Done. Test now pins decoding params and asserts token-by-token match for the first 64 decode tokens plus max-abs on logits.

Sean Gallagher (review): Any risk this changes perf characteristics enough to trip canaries? We should tag the perf events to know we’re on fallback.
Grace Kim (author): Added a structured log field "int8_fused_dequant_gemm_enabled" so benchmark ingestion can segment results. Canary thresholds already allow L40S variance; this should not block correctness.

Connor O'Brien (review): Please confirm this is safe for release/2025.10 and doesn’t require schema changes. Also add a short release note entry for the hotfix.
Grace Kim (author): Confirmed no schema changes; only runtime behavior. Added release note bullet.

Approvals: Hiro Tanaka approved; Arjun Desai approved; Sean Gallagher approved; Connor O'Brien approved.

Merge: Squash merged into release/2025.10 after CI green. Cherry-pick not required.
